pure-announcement.rationale: This is interpretive guidance for reading a metrics dashboard, not a launch or release announcement.

duplicate.rationale: It has substantial content beyond the existing proxy-vs-outcome and first-pass-acceptance concepts — specific cohort/phase mechanics, DAU/WAU thresholds, and ROI-vs-payroll comparison caveats — so a reader of those concepts would still learn something new here.

unfalsifiable.rationale: First-party GitHub documentation describing checkable, reproducible dashboard behaviour and defined metrics.

durability.rationale: Most of the content documents a specific, recently-launched dashboard feature (adoption phases/cohorts shipped roughly three months before this was written per GitHub's own changelog, plus named chat modes and 'recommendation card' UI) — exactly the vendor feature matrix the rubric expects to date within a year; the durable epistemic core (engagement is not productivity, control for confounds) is real but thin next to the dashboard-specific bulk.

actionability.rationale: Each signal pairs with a concrete suggested action — verify license/IDE setup, share internal demos, cross-reference cohort distribution, hold the compensation band constant when comparing periods.

atomicity.rationale: Bundles at least seven distinct interpretation heuristics (DAU/WAU thresholds, chat-mode balance, model adoption, language usage, adoption cohorts, adoption multiplier, ROI-vs-payroll) under a loose 'how to read this dashboard' umbrella rather than one statable idea.
